sections.h2: Assessor and Collector in downtown Hattiesburg
sections.html:
Forrest County keeps a Tax Assessor and a Tax Collector under one roof at 601 N. Main Street. The assessor has to find, classify and value every taxable property each year, a workload of roughly 50,000 parcels of real and personal property.

  • Assessor: (601) 545-6130, mail to P.O. Box 1626, Hattiesburg, MS 39403.
  • Collector: (601) 582-8228, with statements also handled through P.O. Box 1689, Hattiesburg, MS 39403.
  • Parcels appear on TSC Maps, which shows ownership, values, aerial views and legal descriptions.
  • The state requires new aerial photography every ten years, and Forrest County had new photos flown in early 2022.

Assessors must revalue real property at least every four years. The rolls go to the Board of Supervisors, and the public can review them and file protests before the board and the state approve them.

sections.h2: How a Forrest County bill is figured
sections.html:
Take the true value of the property, multiply by the ratio for its class, then multiply by the millage the taxing bodies have set. The Board of Supervisors and the governing boards of Hattiesburg and Petal each contribute a levy. An owner-occupied single-family home is Class I and is assessed at 10% of true value. Other real property is Class II at 15%, personal property is Class III at 15%, public utilities are Class IV at 30%, and motor vehicles are Class V at 30%.

The Department of Revenue publishes combined county and city millage schedules on its property tax data page, which is the place to confirm the rate for your address.

Hattiesburg straddles the Forrest and Lamar county line, so a house on the west side of town can fall under a different assessor, collector and millage than a similar one a mile away. Ask the Forrest County Tax Collector which taxing districts cover your parcel before you quote a monthly cost to a buyer. Hattiesburg, Petal and the county school district each run their own school system, so a Petal address and a Hattiesburg address attend different schools.

sections.h2: Due dates and a freshly recorded deed
sections.html:
Taxes are due on or before February 1 for the property assessed the previous year. If that day falls on a weekend or holiday, you have until the following Monday. One quirk affects sellers: mapping staff work through deeds from the previous year, and it can take up to a year before a new owner's name shows on the land roll.

That lag means a buyer may get a bill in the seller's name, and a seller may keep receiving statements after closing. Whoever signs the settlement statement should give the Tax Collector a new mailing address, since the office wants every change of address or mortgage status reported. Statements go to mortgage companies or to individuals on the mailing list.

Mobile and manufactured homes run on their own clock. A mobile home must be registered within seven days of purchase, and taxes are due within 90 days and then each year after. An owner can declare a mobile home as real property for a fee, which changes how it is assessed.

Applications are taken from January 2 to April 1. It is a one-time filing unless your situation changes, and it does not apply to rental property.

First-time filers bring the recorded deed, the purchase price and down payment, Social Security numbers for owners, and tag numbers for every vehicle, since vehicles must be registered in Forrest County before the application is accepted. A buyer needs to file in their own name, so tell them about the April 1 cutoff.

Talk with the assessor first, then protest to the Board of Supervisors. Owners with a real concern should bring supporting documents such as repair bids or photographs. For a formal appeal, request a hearing with the Board of Supervisors through the Chancery Clerk. The appeal normally must be filed by the first Monday in August before the due date.

Protests are accepted after the rolls are compiled and before the board approves them, so call the assessor to learn when that window opens this year.

sections.h2: What happens if taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
Unpaid real estate taxes put the parcel at risk of a county tax sale, held on either the first Monday in April or the last Monday in August depending on the county.

  • A landowner can redeem within two years after the sale under Miss. Code Ann. 27-45-3.
  • Land that finds no buyer goes to the State, and the Secretary of State handles it.
  • Business personal property has a separate rendition due April 1, with a mandatory 10% penalty for missing it.

Sellers often deal with timing around closing, a roll that has not caught up with a recent deed, and repairs that a conventional buyer's lender may flag. A cash buyer purchases as-is, so those repairs do not delay closing, though liens and unpaid taxes still must be cleared through title.

Before you list or accept an offer, gather the deed, the latest tax statement and any homestead paperwork. Call the Tax Collector at (601) 582-8228 to confirm what is owed, and ask the title company to include the payoff on the closing statement. If the parcel sold at a tax sale, add the redemption amount to the list. The county's population was 79,034 in the 2025 estimate, up from 78,158 in 2020.

Forrest County lies in southeast Mississippi, with Hattiesburg as county seat and largest city. It is part of the Hattiesburg metropolitan area, and Petal is the other city. Interstate 59 and U.S. 11, 49 and 98 run through it. Part of De Soto National Forest falls inside the county, and rural parcels are valued differently from city lots, since agricultural land is valued by soil type and productivity.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Forrest County, MS?
faqs.a: On or before February 1 for property assessed the prior year. If February 1 is a weekend or legal holiday, payment is accepted the next Monday without penalty or interest.

faqs.q: Where is the Forrest County Tax Collector?
faqs.a: 601 N. Main Street in downtown Hattiesburg, phone (601) 582-8228. The Tax Assessor is at the same address, phone (601) 545-6130.

faqs.q: When can I file homestead exemption in Forrest County?
faqs.a: From January 2 to April 1. It is a one-time filing unless something changes, and it does not apply to rental property.

faqs.q: How long does a new deed take to show on the Forrest County roll?
faqs.a: Up to a year after you buy, because mapping staff work the previous year's recorded deeds for the current land roll.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Forrest County house that has back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Back taxes are paid from the sale proceeds at closing, and a title company will confirm the amount. If the parcel was sold at a tax sale, the owner has two years from the sale to redeem.
